chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, who said:
I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about completing the prayer and fasting in the two Sanctuaries, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Complete them, even if it is one prayer.'

key_terms.أَبَا الْحَسَنِ: Abu Al-Hasan (a title for Imam Musa al-Kadhim or Imam Ali al-Rida, contextually often the latter in this specific narration chain)
key_terms.إِتْمَامِ: Completion (of prayer, i.e., praying four rak'ahs instead of two)
key_terms.الْحَرَمَيْنِ: The two Sanctuaries (referring to Masjid al-Haram in Mecca and Masjid al-Nabi in Medina)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on shortening or completing prayers in the two holy sanctuaries according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the ruling for those residing in the two holy sanctuaries (Mecca and Medina), distinguishing their status from typical travelers by mandating the completion of prayers (*tamam*) rather than shortening them (*qasr*). The phrase 'even if it be a single prayer' underscores the obligatory nature of this completion, reflecting the unique spiritual gravity of these sanctuaries where the full ritual is preserved. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence for defining the specific legal status of permanent residents versus transient visitors within these holy cities.
